description: EcoSense is a model listed in Open Energy Platform model and framework factsheets, a public register of energy-system model and framework factsheets under the section "Models", published or maintained by Institute of Energy Economics and Rational Energy Use; University of Stuttgart. EcoSense is a Europe-wide integrated atmospheric dispersion and exposure assessment model which calculates external costs related to the exposure to airborne pollutants with a focus on impacts on human health, following the Impact Pathway approach. Coverage: Switzerland, Norway. Methodical focus: Environmental impact assessment, Air quality management, External costs. Time resolution: annual. Spatial resolution: national states, up to 25' x 25'. Software: PHP, Python, R. The listed link gives the source code or documentation; nothing was downloaded or run. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: this record was written from the Open Energy Platform factsheet only, so the code, documentation and any publication it links were not opened, their current availability was not checked, and the factsheet may lag the project. It can support energy-system planning and scenario studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-oep-factsheet-catalogue.

outputs: EcoSense outputs health impacts with the common metric "Disability Adjusted Life Years" (DALY). DALYs consider both changes in quality of life (due to illness) and losses in life expectancy (due to premature deaths). Impacts can also be monetized, which results in estimates of external costs.
